papers.title: Synaptic GABA dysfunction of thalamocortical neurons impairs sleep spindle morphology and fear extinction.
papers.summary: Using CRISPR-Cas9 knockdown of synaptic GABAA receptors in mouse thalamocortical neurons, this study found that the manipulation abolished the characteristic waxing and waning shape of sleep spindles and impaired extinction of conditioned contextual fear. The results suggest abnormally shaped sleep spindles as a marker of synaptic GABA dysfunction in thalamocortical neurons and disrupted fear extinction.

papers.title: Biophysical modeling of thalamocortical circuit dynamics: species-specific insights into neural synchrony, sleep spindles, and circuit mechanisms.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: A biophysically-grounded computational model incorporating core and matrix thalamocortical pathways, thalamic interneurons, and open/closed/hybrid reticular-thalamic loop configurations was used to investigate species-specific thalamocortical dynamics. Primate-like circuits showed greater stability and synchrony with more regular spindles, whereas rodent-like circuits were more sensitive to parameter changes and exhibited greater variability in spindle structure and timing.

papers.title: Sleep Architecture and Risk-Taking in Adolescents and Young Adults: Independent Contributions of REM Sleep, Sigma Activity, and Morning Cortisol.
papers.summary: In 55 adolescents and young adults, higher REM sleep percentage was associated with better overall performance on a risk-taking task, while greater N2-N3 sigma power was associated with reduced risk-taking under uncertainty; the cortisol awakening response was independently associated with poorer task performance but did not moderate sleep-behavior associations.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Seizure Gating in Sleep-Related Epilepsy: Genes, Channels, Sleep Stages and Circadian Rhythm.
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates epilepsy genetics with sleep neurophysiology to propose that NREM sleep converts continuous molecular defects into state-bound seizures through strengthened thalamocortical coupling, cholinergic withdrawal, arousal destabilization, and circadian modulation, drawing on evidence across nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunits, KCNT1, GATOR1-mTOR, and thalamocortical calcium/HCN channels.

papers.title: Effect of R-R interval normalization on frequency domain analysis of heart rate variability during sleep.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effect of R-R interval normalization on frequency-domain heart rate variability parameters during sleep in 130 participants. Normalization significantly improved differentiation of sleep stages and enhanced slow-wave sleep detection, with the area under the curve for high-frequency-based detection increasing from 0.50 to 0.86.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbance Correlates with Cognitive Impairment Partly via Plasma p-Tau217: ADNI Cross-Sectional Evidence and P301L Mouse Mechanistic Observations.
papers.summary: In ADNI participants (n=230), sleep disturbance was independently linked to higher plasma p-Tau217 and worse cognition, with p-Tau217 partially mediating 44.8% of the sleep-cognition association in MCI and AD but not in cognitively normal individuals; chronic sleep deprivation in P301L tau mice produced cognitive deficits, hippocampal neuronal loss, glial overactivation, and widespread p-Tau217 hyperphosphorylation.

papers.title: Sleep Bursts of Cranial Forces- a Potential Marker of Neurodegenerative Disease.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Sleep Bursts (SBs), brief periodic bursts in cranial forces during sleep, occurred in all 45 subjects but at a lower rate in those with neurodegenerative disease (0.40/min) than controls (0.57/min, p=0.0043), and EEG delta power during SBs was significantly lower in neurodegenerative disease subjects across sleep stages, suggesting SBs may reflect a brain-generated pulsatile component of glymphatic drainage.

papers.title: Clock-Related Genes Mark a Developmental Cortical Maturation Program Associated with Stage-Resolved Responses to Prenatal Immune Activation.
papers.summary: Integrated developmental brain transcriptomes, single-cell atlases, and perturbation datasets to characterize clock-related gene expression in cortical maturation, identifying a postnatal-rising module enriched for synaptic and metabolic processes. Clock-related genes were distributed across neuronal and homeostatic co-expression networks, but the BrainSpan-derived developmental signature showed no significant disruption in prenatal immune activation or ASD postmortem datasets.

papers.title: ET B receptors contribute to synchrony between blood pressure and other peripheral circadian rhythms in the Sprague-Dawley rat.
papers.journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
papers.summary: Telemetry monitoring of Sprague-Dawley rats under constant darkness revealed that chronic ETB receptor blockade delayed mean arterial pressure rhythms and induced desynchrony with heart rate and body temperature rhythms, particularly under high salt diet. The findings support a role for the endothelin system in regulating blood pressure circadian rhythms and maintaining synchrony with peripheral physiological rhythms.

papers.title: TRIM59 attenuates sleep disturbances and improves hippocampal neuronal injury in PCPA-induced sleep-deprived male mice via the NLRP3 signaling pathway.
papers.summary: In PCPA-induced sleep-deprived male mice, hippocampal overexpression of TRIM59 increased 5-HTP, 5-HT, and GABA levels, reduced glutamate, shortened sleep latency, prolonged sleep duration, improved spatial learning and memory, and attenuated hippocampal neuronal injury. TRIM59 also suppressed NLRP3 inflammasome expression, suggesting its neuroprotective effects in sleep disturbances are mediated via the NLRP3 pathway.

papers.title: From EEG Source Localization to Brain Network Analysis: A Computational Neuroscience Perspective.
papers.summary: Reviews the computational framework of EEG source localization, from forward and inverse modeling to source reconstruction, connectivity analysis, and graph-theoretical network modeling, and discusses integration with machine learning for clinical applications. Major methodological challenges including source leakage, model uncertainty, and reproducibility are highlighted.

papers.title: Chronic pain and oscillatory neuroplasticity: Review on impaired compensatory network responses in resting-state electroencephalography.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes resting-state EEG functional connectivity studies in chronic pain and proposes an oscillatory neuroplasticity framework. It reports consistent frequency-specific abnormalities: increased theta connectivity in sensory-limbic pathways, decreased theta in cognitive-control networks, reduced alpha inhibitory maintenance, beta overstabilization of affective-salience networks, and disrupted gamma plasticity.

papers.title: Sleep-dependent alterations in anterior cingulate cortex excitation-inhibition balance link alterations in BOLD-CSF coupling to cognitive performance in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: In 50 OSA patients and 37 controls, this study assessed pre- and post-sleep BOLD-CSF coupling and MRS-derived GABA/Glx in the ACC and PCC. Moderate-to-severe OSA showed weaker pre-sleep global and ACC BOLD-CSF coupling and a disrupted overnight decline in ACC-GABA; greater overnight changes in ACC BOLD-CSF coupling and ACC E/I balance were independently associated with worse cognition, and ACC E/I change moderated the coupling-cognition relationship.

papers.title: Integrative Systems Genomics and Pharmacology Define Shared Immune-Vascular Programs and Prioritize an Experimentally Testable Candidate Linking Sleep Loss to Human Atherosclerosis.
papers.summary: Integrative systems genomics and pharmacology analysis of sleep restriction and carotid plaque transcriptomes showed resolution-dependent convergence, with 35 of 50 redundancy-collapsed programs concordant across compartments, and prioritized SF3A3 as a candidate linking sleep loss to atherosclerosis via Mendelian randomization and colocalization.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Diagnostics Using Photoplethysmography (PPG): Beyond SpO2 and Heart Rate.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes AI-based photoplethysmography applications for cardiovascular, respiratory, sleep, hemodynamic, pregnancy-related, and portal hypertension assessment, finding evidence supporting blood pressure estimation, atrial fibrillation detection, and other uses, while identifying motion artifacts, skin-pigmentation bias, and limited external validation as barriers to clinical translation.

papers.title: Multidomain Electroencephalography Biomarker Fusion for Machine Learning-Based Dementia Classification.
papers.summary: This study evaluated multidomain EEG biomarkers for classifying Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls using a Random Forest classifier with explainable AI. The full model achieved 96% training and 92% test accuracy; removing entropy features increased test accuracy to 94%, with entropy showing the lowest classification contribution.

papers.title: Physical exercise as a modulator of the sleep-obesity interaction: metabolic, neuroendocrine and circadian mechanisms.
papers.summary: This review discusses how physical exercise modulates the multidirectional relationship between sleep and obesity through metabolic, neuroendocrine, and circadian mechanisms. It highlights exercise as a non-photic zeitgeber that may interrupt the vicious cycle linking obesity and sleep disturbances, improving metabolic health and reducing comorbidity burden.

papers.title: Molecular Drivers of Cognitive Decline and Neuroprotection in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes molecular pathways in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) that drive neurodegeneration (e.g., SUMOylation dysregulation, toll-like receptor signaling, inflammasome overactivation) and endogenous neuroprotective adaptations (e.g., erythropoietin upregulation, anaerobic glycolysis shifts, neurotrophic factors), proposing a 'neuroprotective reserve' framework to describe the dynamic balance between injury and protection.

papers.title: Effects of MRI-Navigated Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation on Task Performance, Subjective Workload, and EEG Responses During Prolonged Simulated Flight: A Randomized Crossover Study.
papers.summary: In a randomized, order-balanced, within-subject crossover study of 25 healthy men during 60-min simulated flight, MRI-navigated active iTBS over the left DLPFC increased composite performance scores in later phases and reduced NASA-TLX workload in Phase 3 compared to sham and no stimulation, with concurrent EEG showing relative reductions in frontocentral theta and fronto-parieto-occipital alpha power.

papers.title: Acute Sleep Deprivation Is Associated with Altered F-Wave Temporal Dynamics and Nasalis Repetitive Nerve Stimulation Responses: A Paired Electrophysiological Study.
papers.summary: In a prospective paired within-participant study of 30 healthy resident physicians, acute overnight sleep deprivation was associated with increased F-wave maximum latency and chronodispersion, decreased persistence, and a small directional shift toward decrement in nasalis repetitive nerve stimulation responses, though RNS values remained within physiological limits.

papers.title: Thermosomnia: Consequences of rising temperatures and climate change for clinical sleep disorders.
papers.summary: This review introduces the term "thermosomnia" to characterize the impact of rising ambient temperatures on clinical sleep disorders. It synthesizes evidence that elevated temperatures exacerbate obstructive sleep apnoea and insomnia symptoms, threaten treatment adherence, and are likely worsened by climate change, disproportionately affecting vulnerable groups.

papers.title: Why Seizures Break Through: Distinguishing Background Susceptibility From Proximal Precipitants in Patients With Epilepsy.
papers.summary: This narrative review distinguishes background susceptibility from proximal precipitants in breakthrough seizures. It finds that prior seizure burden, difficulty achieving remission, neurological impairment, treatment history, and epilepsy etiology reflect greater background susceptibility, whereas nonadherence has strong mechanistic evidence and sleep deprivation, stress, infection, alcohol, and pregnancy vary in evidentiary strength.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic EEG Signatures in ASD and ADHD: A Comparative Review of Computational Biomarkers and Neuromodulatory Interventions.
papers.summary: This comparative review synthesized EEG findings from 68 studies in ASD and ADHD, identifying shared features such as low-frequency theta excess, reduced alpha modulation, and flattened aperiodic slopes, while disorder-specific signatures included a 'U-shaped' spectral profile and elevated epileptiform activity in ASD and frontally pronounced theta/beta ratio elevation in ADHD; it proposes a biomarker-informed framework for intervention selection.

papers.title: Pain Mechanisms in Fibromyalgia: An Integrative Narrative Review of Central, Peripheral, Neuroimmune, and Psychobiological Factors.
papers.summary: This integrative narrative review synthesizes mechanisms of pain in fibromyalgia, emphasizing central sensitization, impaired descending pain modulation, neurochemical dysregulation, small-fiber pathology, neuroimmune processes, and psychobiological modulators. It concludes that fibromyalgia is a heterogeneous nociplastic pain syndrome arising from interacting central, peripheral, neuroimmune, autonomic, and psychobiological mechanisms that vary across patients.

papers.title: Iron Deficiency and Human Brain Electrophysiology Across the Lifespan: A Systematic and Mechanistic Review of Resting EEG, Event-Related Potentials, and Treatment Responsiveness.
papers.summary: This systematic and mechanistic review synthesized EEG findings across the lifespan and found that iron deficiency is commonly associated with increased slow-wave activity, reduced alpha activity, delayed sensory and cognitive processing, prolonged P300 and N2 latencies, and altered frontal alpha asymmetry, with iron supplementation improving some spectral and ERP outcomes though recovery was variable.

papers.title: Ramadan fasting and thyroid function: a narrative review of physiological adaptation and clinical management.
papers.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes evidence on Ramadan fasting and thyroid function in healthy, hypothyroid, and hyperthyroid individuals. It reports that Ramadan fasting preserves hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis function in healthy adults, may increase post-Ramadan TSH in levothyroxine-treated hypothyroid patients with stable FT4, and that evidence in hyperthyroidism is limited and based on expert opinion.

papers.title: Sleep-disordered breathing, sleep duration, and 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure in subjective short-sleeping adults.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional secondary analysis of a behavioral sleep extension trial evaluated associations between sleep apnea severity, objective sleep duration, and 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure in short-sleeping adults with elevated in-office blood pressure. Greater apnea-hypopnea index was associated with higher mean diastolic blood pressure after adjustment (0.92 mmHg per 10 events/hour, p=0.027), and a significant AHI by sleep duration interaction was found for systolic non-dipping.

papers.title: Morin-Loaded PLGA-Chitosan Nanoparticles Attenuate PTZ-Induced Seizure-Related Behavioral, Biochemical, and Transcriptional Changes in Male Rats.
papers.summary: Morin-loaded PLGA-chitosan nanoparticles (Morin-PLGA-CS NPs) were synthesized and tested in male Wistar rats for anticonvulsant and anxiolytic effects. Compared with free morin, the nanoparticles prolonged PTZ-induced seizure latency (137.2 s vs. 114.5 s), reduced cortical and hippocampal IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α, increased hippocampal Nrf2 and HO-1 mRNA, and decreased GFAP and Iba1 mRNA.

papers.title: Evaluation of the Intervention Effect of Bifidobacterium longum on Constipation in Sleep-Deprived Mice.
papers.summary: Sleep-deprived mice were used to evaluate whether Bifidobacterium longum 151-1 and BN-BB01 alleviate constipation via gut-brain axis mechanisms. Sleep deprivation impaired intestinal motility and barrier function, reduced excitatory gastrointestinal hormones and neurotransmitters, and altered short-chain fatty acids; Bifidobacterium longum reversed these abnormalities, increased GPR41/GPR109A, BDNF, and GDNF, inhibited HDAC, and shifted microbiota composition.

papers.title: Correlation Analysis of Sleep Quality and Heart Rate Variability in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
papers.summary: This prospective observational cohort study of 95 cardiac surgery patients examined correlations between perioperative sleep quality and heart rate variability. It found that patients with poor sleep quality had significantly lower HF, SDNN, SDANN, PNN50, and RMSSD at all time points, and that these HRV parameters were significantly negatively correlated with sleep disturbance, with PNN50 at 1 day postoperatively showing the strongest correlation (r=-0.78).

papers.title: The Role of Sleep Studies to Predict Post-Operative Outcomes in Children with Medical Complexity.
papers.summary: This retrospective study analyzed 357 children with medical complexity who underwent spinal arthrodesis for scoliosis correction, with preoperative sleep studies performed in 119 patients to identify sleep-disordered breathing or nocturnal hypoventilation. Sleep study findings guided initiation of non-invasive ventilation in 20 patients and CPAP in 2, and postoperative respiratory support was frequently required, with median PICU stay 4.0 days, median invasive ventilation 15.5 hours, one tracheostomy, and no perioperative deaths; the authors conclude sleep studies influence perioperative respiratory management but prospective controlled confirmation is needed.

papers.title: The Circadian-Melatonin Axis in Bone Remodeling: Receptor-Dependent Signaling, Receptor-Independent Actions, and Translational Constraints.
papers.summary: This narrative review appraises whether the circadian-melatonin axis contributes to bone remodeling and osteoporosis, focusing on receptor dependence, exposure concentration, and study architecture. It concludes that many antiosteoclastic and antioxidant effects occur at micromolar concentrations far above nocturnal plasma levels, that conventional oral doses likely engage receptor-mediated osteoblast pathways rather than reproduce high-dose effects, and that melatonin cannot currently be recommended for osteoporosis treatment.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances and Their Associations with Child and Family Quality of Life in School-Aged Children Born Before 32 Weeks of Gestation: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional comparative study found that school-aged children born before 32 weeks of gestation had significantly higher total Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC) scores than term-born peers, particularly for difficulties initiating and maintaining sleep and sleep-wake transition disorders. Sleep disturbances were independently associated with poorer parental quality of life, regardless of children's quality of life.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Coordinated Gliovascular Remodeling Across Diffuse Glioma Grades.
papers.summary: Integrated transcriptomic analysis of TCGA and CGGA cohorts quantified eight gliovascular unit components and found coordinated grade-associated remodeling across diffuse glioma grades. Lower-grade tumors showed greater homeostatic astrocyte- and endfoot-associated programs, whereas higher-grade tumors showed increased inflammatory, ECM-remodeling, basement membrane-remodeling, and angiogenic signatures; these patterns were spatially compartmentalized in GBM but not independently associated with overall survival.

papers.title: Effects of Virtual Pedagogical Agents and Instructional Content Type on Learners' Experience in Online Learning: Evidence from Behavioral, Eye-Tracking, and EEG Data.
papers.summary: This 2x2 mixed-design study with 40 university students used questionnaires, eye tracking, and EEG to test how virtual pedagogical agent type (human-like vs. non-human) and instructional content type (traditional knowledge vs. interest-oriented popular science) affect online learning experience. The interaction significantly influenced learning experience: human-like agents produced higher satisfaction, greater emotional attachment, and lower psychological distance for traditional knowledge, whereas non-human agents yielded better knowledge recall, higher satisfaction, stronger emotional attachment, and lower psychological distance for interest-oriented content; EEG FCz spectral power varied with the combination but showed broadband increases across theta, alpha, beta, and gamma, limiting

papers.title: Peer Victimization and Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Among Chinese Adolescents: Moderating Roles of Teacher Emotional Support and Parent-Child Cohesion.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 4128 Chinese adolescents, peer victimization was significantly correlated with non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), and this relationship was mediated by sleep quality. Teacher emotional support, but not parent-child cohesion, remained a significant moderator of the sleep quality-NSSI pathway when both moderators were examined simultaneously.

papers.title: Traumatic Bereavement Among Incarcerated Women: Understanding and Responding to Complex Grief After the Death of a Child.
papers.summary: This conceptual manuscript examines traumatic bereavement after the death of a child among incarcerated women, integrating the Dual Process Model of Coping and meaning-making frameworks to explain how carceral restrictions on privacy, autonomy, family contact, mourning rituals, and clinical support constrain adaptive grief processing. It specifies testable propositions and a framework for notification, stabilization, and continuing bereavement support, while identifying protective pathways such as family connection, peer support, cultural and spiritual practices, and clinical care.

papers.title: High Psychosocial Impact of Complications, Suboptimal Coping Strategies, and Burnout among Spine Surgeons.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 50 spine surgeons found that nearly all reported psychological suffering after a serious surgical complication, with common symptoms including guilt (42%), depression (38%), and anxiety (36%). Burnout-domain symptoms were prevalent, with moderate-to-severe exhaustion in 44%, depersonalization in 40%, and poor professional accomplishment in 48%; anxiety after a complication was associated with higher burnout symptoms.

papers.title: The Impact of Allergic Rhinitis on Australian Adults in an Urban Setting: A Qualitative Exploration.
papers.summary: This qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with 38 adults with allergic rhinitis in urban Victoria, Australia, identified five themes including that allergic rhinitis disrupts quality of life through poor sleep, emotional strain, social limitations, and reduced productivity. Participants also described limited awareness and barriers in healthcare access hindering effective management.

papers.title: Homoeopathic Management of Hypothyroidism: A Narrative Review of Reported Clinical Experience, Individualised Prescribing, and Research Gaps.
papers.summary: This narrative review of 53 sources found that the available evidence on homoeopathic management of hypothyroidism is heterogeneous and predominantly uncontrolled, with reported improvements that cannot be assumed to represent treatment-specific effects. The authors conclude that a scientifically established mechanism for specific clinical effects has not been demonstrated and that homoeopathic care should not replace or delay indicated thyroid hormone therapy.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
